name: Huawei OSTA O1 Pro
gaming_notes: The Kirin 9030S with a 120Hz 1.5K OLED and a 7,000mAh battery handles demanding titles well, and the wide 16:9.5 screen suits games and video; this is a camera-and-AI-first phone rather than a dedicated gaming device.

name: Huawei nova 16s Pro
gaming_notes: The Kirin 9010S with a 1-120Hz LTPO OLED runs demanding titles smoothly, though this is a camera-first phone — there is no active cooling or dedicated gaming hardware.

name: Huawei nova 16s
gaming_notes: The Kirin 8020 with a 120Hz OLED handles popular titles at sensible settings, but this is a camera-first phone, not a gaming phone — there is no active cooling or gaming trigger hardware.

name: Samsung Galaxy A18 LTE
gaming_notes: A budget chipset and 90Hz AMOLED keep casual games smooth, but this is a longevity-first phone, not a gaming one.

name: Samsung Galaxy A08 LTE
gaming_notes: The Helio G99+ runs popular titles like PUBG Mobile and Free Fire smoothly at balanced settings on the 90Hz display.

name: Sharp AQUOS sense11
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 with a 1–240Hz Pro IGZO OLED handles popular titles smoothly at high settings, and the 5,000mAh battery lasts through long gaming sessions.

name: Vivo V80 FE
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7400 Turbo is a strong mid-range gaming chip — popular titles run smoothly at high settings, and the 120Hz AMOLED display keeps gameplay fluid. The 7,000mAh battery easily lasts through long gaming sessions.

name: Oppo Reno 17 Pro
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 8550 Super is a strong upper-mid-range chip — heavy games run smoothly on high settings with 120fps support, and the 7,250mAh battery keeps long sessions going.

name: Oppo Reno 17
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 is a powerful mid-range chip — heavy games run smoothly on high settings, and Oppo adds 120fps gaming support. The 8,000mAh battery makes long gaming sessions easy too.

name: Redmi 17 5G
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 4 Gen 5 is a budget-tier 5G chip — smooth for casual games and daily play on the 120Hz display, but demanding titles need medium-low settings. The 7,500mAh battery is the real gaming asset: very long sessions without a charger.

name: Redmi 17
gaming_notes: The Helio G91-Ultra is an entry-level chip — fine for casual and light multiplayer games on medium settings, but heavy titles will stutter. As with the 5G sibling, the 7,500mAh battery means all-day gaming without charging.

name: Vivo V80
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 is a solid midrange gaming chip that runs popular titles smoothly at medium-high settings; the 144Hz 1.5K AMOLED display makes gameplay feel fluid.
